attributes.context: Article XXV – Demand Flow Technology states that Demand Flow Technology is a prerequisite for consideration of manufacturing in La Crosse and makes La Crosse more cost-competitive in the industry.

The 1993 Amendment section on Demand Flow Technology notes that American Standard facilities are converting to Demand Flow Manufacturing Technology to eliminate nonvalue-added activities and that cooperation is a prerequisite for La Crosse manufacturing of redesigned products.

It appears in the Requirements for Upgrade section and contrasts with a prior statement that temporary performance of a stand-alone higher-classification job is compensated under Article VIII, Paragraph 75.

extraction_text: However, consistent with Demand Flow Technology principles, employees may be required to perform duties at adjacent work stations for short periods of time that may be in a higher or lower classification without having their rate of pay adjusted.

attributes.context: The passage is located in the Requirements for Upgrade section, immediately after a statement that employees temporarily performing a stand-alone job in a higher classification are compensated under Article VIII, Paragraph 74, and before statements that the Company will establish distribution percentages and hold semi-annual workforce distribution meetings.

extraction_text: However, consistent with Demand Flow Technology principles, employees may be required to perform duties at adjacent work stations for short periods of time that may be in a higher or lower classification without having their rate of pay adjusted. This principle of "one up, one down," is essential to Demand Flow.

attributes.context: The preceding text explains that Schedule E time progressions are based on "of working time" and may be adjusted for layoff, long leave, and leave of absence.

The Company is implementing a new time and attendance recordkeeping system which will aid in the tracking "of time worked," as well as provide timely response to requests for certain types of personnel information.

The Company will provide the Union Office with two (2) terminals and one (1) printer so direct viewing can be made by the Shop Committee of non-confidential hourly employee information, i.e., vacation, absentee records, training records, etc.

extraction_text:
The Company and the Union agree that it is to both their mutual benefit and a sound economic and social goal to utilize the most efficient machines, processes, methods and/or materials. In this way, the Company will be able to compete effectively in the marketplace and, thereby, provide economically secure jobs for its employees.

The Company further agrees to meet with the Union in order to evaluate the impact of technological changes on all employees. Where possible the Company will assist in reassigning employees in affected areas based on seniority and ability.

attributes.context: The surrounding section states that American Standard Inc. and its facilities are converting to Demand Flow Manufacturing Technology intended to eliminate nonvalue-added activities, and that doing so makes La Crosse more cost-competitive.
